previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation, severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and right leg swelling. He had presented to the ED multiple times in the prior week. Initial evaluation revealed pulmonary edema and pleural effusions, with markedly elevated BNP, leading to IV diuresis. An echocardiogram showed progression of aortic stenosis to severe, managed conservatively. Thoracentesis was performed, removing 1L of transudative fluid, which improved his breathing. Cellulitis of the right leg was treated with IV vancomycin followed by oral doxycycline. Acute kidney injury and hyponatremia were noted but stabilized. Warfarin was held temporarily and restarted, though INR remained subtherapeutic at discharge, requiring ongoing monitoring. The patient improved clinically and was discharged to extended care with instructions to monitor weight, symptoms, and INR, and to continue leg elevation and antibiotics.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
